title: Bytes, Hex and Addresses: cheat sheet

blocks.title: The big idea
blocks.body: Memory is a row of numbered bytes. Each byte has an address. Everything your program holds is built from bytes.

blocks.title: Bits, bytes, hex
items: One hex digit = 4 bits, a byte = 2 hex digits
Hex digits: 0-9 then A=10 to F=15

blocks.title: Operators
items: `sizeof x` is the size in bytes

blocks.title: Sizes used here (64-bit)
items: Items in an array: `sizeof a / sizeof a[0]`

blocks.body: Addresses differ between machines and runs. Print them to learn, but never rely on a value.
